create.name: Mike Sheehy
create.bio:
Mike Sheehy is a Dublin-based mindfulness teacher and the founder of BíMeditation, a secular practice he set up to bring meditation into ordinary working life. He came to teaching from business rather than from a monastery: over more than thirty years he has held leadership posts in technology, operations and organisational change, and he has kept up his own meditation practice for well over a decade. He says he teaches because sitting still each day has helped him through his own pressures, and he speaks about it in plain, down-to-earth terms.

Under the name The Awareness Advantage he gives talks and ninety-minute workshops for companies, staff wellbeing programmes, enterprise offices and founder groups, looking at how noticing our habits and reactions shapes attention, choices and the way we deal with each other. For individuals he leads a thirty-minute guided meditation online every Wednesday evening, and he records guided sitting practices and an unusual series of running and walking meditations, from twenty minutes to an hour, for people who find it easier to settle while moving. A free starter kit with two short practices and video tips is on his website, and his guided meditations can also be heard on Insight Timer.

courses.title: Midweek Online Guided Meditation
courses.description: A thirty-minute guided mindfulness session held live online every Wednesday at 8pm Irish time. Each session is booked individually and needs no experience.

courses.title: The Awareness Advantage: Talks & Workshops
courses.description: Talks and ninety-minute workshops for teams, leaders and founder groups on how awareness affects attention, decisions and communication at work. Each session mixes short practices with discussion and can be adapted to the audience.

courses.title: 30mins Running/Walking Meditation
courses.description: A guided audio for a run or walk that uses the contact of each footstep with the ground as the anchor for attention. Versions from twenty minutes to an hour are sold on the same shop, and the file is sent by email after purchase.

free_resources.title: Free Mindfulness Meditation Starter Kit
free_resources.description: A starting point for beginners: a six-minute sitting practice and a fifteen-minute running or walking practice to play or download, with short video tips on sleepiness, a busy mind and restlessness.

free_resources.title: 6-Minute Guided Mindfulness Meditation
free_resources.description: A short sitting practice that settles attention on the breath, suitable for a first try at meditation or a pause in the working day.

free_resources.title: 20 Minute Guided Mindfulness Meditation
free_resources.description: A longer guided mindfulness sit of about twenty minutes, for days when there is more time to settle and stay with the breath.

flags: Base: Dublin comes from his Insight Timer profile; his own site names no city (the file name of a speaking photo on his site mentions Swords, Co. Dublin).
Secular, workplace-focused mindfulness (performance, focus, leadership) rather than a spiritual lineage; a human may judge whether he fits Spiritpedia.

Health wording: his Insight Timer bio frames the work around stress, anxiety, low mood and collective trauma in Ireland, and the shop says meditation can improve sleep and memory; the bio and items avoid that framing.
Insight Timer shows no play counts, so the two tracks chosen are the shortest and longest sitting practices rather than the most played.
Availability local_online: he gives in-person workshops in the Dublin area and runs his weekly session online.
His YouTube channel has five clips, all under two minutes, so no videos are listed; youtube_url kept for the channel.
left_out: YouTube clips (Why Meditate, Tips #1-#4): all under two minutes.
Other paid downloads (10, 16, 26 and 30-minute sitting meditations, 20 to 60-minute running/walking versions): one representative item kept to avoid near-duplicates.
Insight Timer running/walking tracks: duplicates of the paid downloads.
Speaker pack and 'Insights' blog posts: not teaching items.
